effective_date_basis: The date in the order, or the end of the committee's authorizing resolution or Congress; otherwise a stated gap.
ending_pattern: The order opens returns to inspection by a named committee or official for an investigation, under a specific Revenue Act section. It ends when the inspection or the investigating body's authority ends, or on a date in its own text; standing orders for a class of officials (for example State officers) are outliers.

exceptions_savings.assessment: Information already inspected is an accrued effect.

legal_effect: Research pattern only. A type rule never fills a judgment field, establishes an end, a date, a status or savings for any order, and never substitutes for reading the order's own text.
outlier_conditions: The order's own text (not only the WPA summary or APP title) does not match the type, or the held text is another order's.
The order does more than the type's single act (a second operative clause of another kind).
A later order or statute amends, extends, revokes or revives it before the candidate end.
The order states its own effective date, duration, condition or termination that differs from the pattern.
The order prescribes general regulations for inspection rather than a single grant.
A standing class order (State officers, all years) rather than a single committee grant.
The committee's authority was renewed in a later Congress, which extends the inspection.
Statutory replacement of the authority (IRC 1939 s.55; IRC 1954 s.6103; the Tax Reform Act of 1976 rewrite of s.6103): candidate authority-lapse ends, not presumed ends.
quoted_clause:
By virtue of the authority vested in me by section 257 (a) of the Revenue Act
of 1926 (ch. 27, 44 Stat. 9, 51), section 55 of the Revenue Act of 1928 (ch. 852, 45
Stat. 791, 809), and section 55 of the Revenue Act of 1932 (ch. 209, 47 Stat. 169, 189),
it is hereby ordered that tax returns shall be open to inspection by the Special Com-
mittee Investigating the Munitions Industry, United States Senate, authorized by
Senate Resolution 206, Seventy-third Congress, to investigate the manufacture of
and traffic in arms, munitions, and other implements of war, such inspection to be
in accordance and upon compliance with the rules and regulations prescribed by
the Secretary of the Treasury and approved by the President under date of De-
cember 13, 1932, as amended under date of August 3, 1933, as further amended
under dates of October 18, 1933, and May 21, 1934, and as further amended this date.

The committee's authorizing resolution or term (shared source).
The Revenue Act section the order relies on, and its later replacements.

scope.note: Membership is a machine lead; each order is decided by an agent, row by row.

source.custody_limit: Exemplar text is a held copy graded machine_read_government_printed_copy; it illustrates the type's wording and is not an authenticated original.
